full_judgment:
Md Rezaul Masan, J: This Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 13-12-2021 (decree signed on 15-12,-2021), passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Gaibandha, in Family Appeal No.49 of 2020, disallowing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 8-10- 2020 (decree signed on 14-10-2020), passed by the Judge of the Family Court, Gaibandha, in Family Suit No.2 of 2020, should not be set-aside, and/or such other or further order or orders, as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 5. The trial court, after hearing the parties, has decreed the suit and granted relief as prayed for, vide it's judgment and decree dated 8-10- 2020. 

 6. Against the judgment and decree of the trial court, the defendant has preferred Family Appeal No,49 of 2020, which was heard by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Gaibandha, who has dismissed the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree of the trial court, vide it's judgment and order dated 13-12-2021. 

 7. Being aggrieved thereby and dissatisfied with the said judgment and decree of the appellate court, the defendant-appellant has filed this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and obtained the instant Rule. 

 8. Learned Advocate Mr Khondker Shamsul Hoque Reza has appeared on behalf of the defendant-appellant--petitioner. He submits that, the marriage cannot be made twice between the plaintiff No.1 and the defendant_ Their only contention is that, the defendant admits the marriage that was solenamized on 5-4-2012 (Exhibit C), wherein dower money was fixed at Taka 1,00,001. The defendant does not admit the Nikaimama that was registered on 9-4-2012 (Exhibit 1), wherein dower money has shown as Taka 3,00,000. He also submits that, the defendant has been paying maintenance for the minors children. But, the trial court without considering the oral and documentary evidence has decreed the suit, while the appellate court, as the last court of fact, did not independently assess the evidence on record and has mechanically concurred with the findings of fact of the trial court and thereby it has committed error of law in passing the impugned judgment and decree that has resulted in error in the decision and has occasioned failure of justice. He also submits that, the defendant has already disputed Taka 1,14,000 as dower money and therefore, the rest of the dower money shall be recovered as per law. He prays for making the Rule absolute. 

 9. Learned Advocate Mr td Mizanur Rahman has appeared on behalf of the plaintiffs-respondents-opposite parties. He submits that, both the courts below have assessed the evidence on record and have concurrently found that the plaintiff was entitled to get her dower money on the basis Nikahnaina, registered on 9-4-2012, and both the courts below have also found that, the plaintiffs are entitled to get their maintenance as well as the cost of Medical bills that arose at time of birth of minor plaintiff No.3. He also submits that, there is no case of misreading and non-reading of any evidence and in passing the judgments and decrees of both the courts. He also submits that, both the parties are consented to execute the Nikahnama dated 9-4-2012 and, therefore, the defendant cannot deny his liability to pay dower money as per Nikahnama dated 9-4-012 (Exhibit 1). He concludes that, this Rule has no merit and the same may be discharged. 

 The impugned judgment and decree 13-12-2021, passed by the appellate court in Family Appeal No.49 of 2020, is hereby up held. 

 The defendant should pay the rest amount to the plaintiff No. 1, the cost of maintenance as well as the medical bills as per the decree of the court below. 

 Considering the practical cost of living, the maintenance is fixed as the rate of Taka 3,000 per month and the decree shall stand modified accordingly.
